name: Wizard Spider
summary: Wizard Spider is a Russia-based financially motivated threat group originally known for the creation and deployment of TrickBot since at least 2016. Wizard Spider possesses a diverse arsenal of tools and has conducted ransomware campaigns against a variety of organizations, ranging from major corporations to hospitals.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has leveraged ProtonMail email addresses in ransom notes when delivering Ryuk ransomware.

Wizard Spider has utilized tools such as Empire, Cobalt Strike, Cobalt Strike, Rubeus, AdFind, BloodHound, Metasploit, Advanced IP Scanner, Nirsoft PingInfoView, and SoftPerfect Network Scanner for targeting efforts.
Wizard Spider has obtained code signing certificates signed by DigiCert, GlobalSign, and COMOOD for malware payloads.

cites.name: DFIR Ryuk 2 Hour Speed Run November 2020

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has sent phishing emails containing a link to an actor-controlled Google Drive document or other free online file hosting services.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has used administrative accounts, including Domain Admin, to move laterally within a victim network.
Wizard Spider has used spearphishing attachments to deliver Microsoft documents containing macros or PDFs containing malicious links to download either Emotet, Bokbot, TrickBot, or Bazar.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has used valid credentials for privileged accounts with the goal of accessing domain controllers.
Emotet: Emotet can brute force a local admin password, then use it to facilitate lateral movement.
Wizard Spider has accessed victim networks by using stolen credentials to access the corporate VPN infrastructure.
Wizard Spider has used `cmd.exe` to execute commands on a victim's machine.
Wizard Spider has used scheduled tasks to establish persistence for TrickBot and other malware.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses the Windows API call, CreateProcessW(), to manage execution flow. TrickBot has also used `Nt*` API functions to perform Process Injection.
Wizard Spider has used macros to execute PowerShell scripts to download malware on victim's machines. It has also used PowerShell to execute commands and move laterally through a victim network.

Wizard Spider has used `services.exe` to execute scripts and executables during lateral movement within a victim's network. Wizard Spider has also used batch scripts that leverage PsExec to execute a previously transferred ransomware payload on a victim's network.
Wizard Spider has used WMI and LDAP queries for network discovery and to move laterally. Wizard Spider has also used batch scripts to leverage WMIC to deploy ransomware.
Wizard Spider has used batch scripts that utilizes WMIC to execute a BITSAdmin transfer of a ransomware payload to each compromised machine.
Wizard Spider has lured victims into clicking a malicious link delivered through spearphishing.
Wizard Spider has lured victims to execute malware with spearphishing attachments containing macros to download either Emotet, Bokbot, TrickBot, or Bazar.
SystemBC: SystemBC has leveraged VBScript to execute malicious code.
Anchor: Anchor can install itself as a cron job.
Empire: Empire uses a command-line interface to interact with systems.
Anchor: Anchor can execute payloads via shell scripting.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use Python to perform execution.
Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike System Profiler can use JavaScript to perform reconnaissance actions.
Empire: Empire can use built-in modules to abuse trusted utilities like MSBuild.exe.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can exploit Oracle Java vulnerabilities for execution, including CVE-2011-3544, CVE-2013-2465, CVE-2012-4681, and CVE-2013-2460.
TrickBot: TrickBot used COM to setup scheduled task for persistence.
Empire: Empire contains modules that can discover and exploit various DLL hijacking opportunities.
Empire: Empire has a dylib hijacker module that generates a malicious dylib given the path to a legitimate dylib of a vulnerable application.
Empire: Empire contains modules that can discover and exploit path interception opportunities in the PATH environment variable.
Empire: Empire contains modules that can discover and exploit search order hijacking vulnerabilities.
Empire: Empire contains modules that can discover and exploit unquoted path vulnerabilities.
Wizard Spider has installed TrickBot as a service named ControlServiceA in order to establish persistence.
Wizard Spider has established persistence via the Registry key `HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` and a shortcut within the startup folder.
Wizard Spider has created and used new accounts within a victim's Active Directory environment to maintain persistence.

Wizard Spider has modified the Registry key `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest` by setting the `UseLogonCredential` registry value to `1` in order to force credentials to be stored in clear text in memory.
Wizard Spider has created local administrator accounts to maintain persistence in compromised networks.
Wizard Spider has established persistence using Userinit by adding the Registry key HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon.
Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper contains an implementation of an SSP.
Bazar: Bazar can establish persistence by writing shortcuts to the Windows Startup folder.

Mimikatz: The Mimikatz credential dumper has been extended to include Skeleton Key domain controller authentication bypass functionality. The `LSADUMP::ChangeNTLM` and `LSADUMP::SetNTLM` modules can also manipulate the password hash of an account without knowing the clear text value.
Net: The `net localgroup` and `net group` commands in Net can be used to add existing users to local and domain groups.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to use an Excel Workbook to execute additional code by enabling Office to trust macros and execute code without user permission.
Ryuk: Ryuk has used Wake-on-Lan to power on turned off systems for lateral movement.
TrickBot: TrickBot can implant malicious code into a compromised device's firmware.
Empire: Empire can leverage WMI debugging to remotely replace binaries like sethc.exe, Utilman.exe, and Magnify.exe with cmd.exe.
Wizard Spider has used process injection to execute payloads to escalate privileges.
Wizard Spider has injected malicious DLLs into memory with read, write, and execute permissions.

procedures.text: TrickBot: TrickBot injects into the svchost.exe process.
Empire: Empire can exploit vulnerabilities such as MS16-032 and MS16-135.
Ryuk: Ryuk has attempted to adjust its token privileges to have the `SeDebugPrivilege`.
Emotet: Emotet has the ability to duplicate the user’s token. For example, Emotet may use a variant of Google’s ProtoBuf to send messages that specify how code will be executed.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `MISC::AddSid` module can append any SID or user/group account to a user's SID-History. Mimikatz also utilizes SID-History Injection to expand the scope of other components such as generated Kerberos Golden Tickets and DCSync beyond a single domain.
Empire: Empire includes various modules to attempt to bypass UAC for escalation of privileges.
Bazar: Bazar can inject into a target process using process doppelgänging.
Empire: Empire can use `Invoke-RunAs` to make tokens.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can make tokens from known credentials.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can spawn processes with alternate PPIDs.
Empire: Empire can use `New-GPOImmediateTask` to modify a GPO that will install and execute a malicious Scheduled Task/Job.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use `sudo` to run a command.
TrickBot: TrickBot decodes the configuration data and modules.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses non-descriptive names to hide functionality.
TrickBot: TrickBot leverages a custom packer to obfuscate its functionality.
Wizard Spider has used file deletion to remove some modules and configurations from an infected host after use.
Wizard Spider used Base64 encoding to obfuscate an Empire service and PowerShell commands.

Wizard Spider has used scheduled tasks to install TrickBot, using task names to appear legitimate such as WinDotNet, GoogleTask, or Sysnetsf. It has also used common document file names for other malware binaries.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses an AES CBC (256 bits) encryption algorithm for its loader and configuration files.
Wizard Spider has utilized `rundll32.exe` to deploy ransomware commands with the use of WebDAV.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used `printf` and file I/O loops to delay process execution as part of API hammering.
SystemBC: SystemBC has downloaded a text file into memory and set the area of memory via the VirtualProtect call. Then, SystemBC has executed the file via the CreateThread call.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent has the ability to add bytes to change the file hash.
TrickBot: The TrickBot downloader has used an icon to appear as a Microsoft Word document.
Bazar: The Bazar loader has named malicious shortcuts "adobe" and mimicked communications software.
Empire: Empire can timestomp any files or payloads placed on a target machine to help them blend in.
Bazar: Bazar's loader can delete scheduled tasks created by a previous instance of the malware.

SystemBC: SystemBC has checked if the last characters of DNS server names end in.bit before initializing C2 communication. SystemBC has identified running processes associated with anti-virus solutions to include `a2guard.exe` to determine whether it executes or not.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used a hidden VNC (hVNC) window to monitor the victim and collect information stealthily.
Diavol: Diavol has obfuscated its main code routines within bitmap images as part of its anti-analysis techniques.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike includes a capability to modify the Beacon payload to eliminate known signatures or unpacking methods.
Bazar: Bazar can hash then resolve API calls at runtime.
Emotet: Emotet has dropped an embedded executable at `%Temp%\setup.exe`. Additionally, Emotet may embed entire code into other files.
Bazar: The Bazar loader has used dual-extension executable files such as PreviewReport.DOC.exe.
Net: The `net use \\system\share /delete` command can be used in Net to remove an established connection to a network share.
Emotet: Emotet uses RegSvr32 to execute the DLL payload.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent uses the last 64 bytes of the binary to compute a mutex name. If the generated name is invalid, it will default to the generic `mymutex`.
Bazar: Bazar can attempt to overload sandbox analysis by sending 1550 calls to `printf`.
Dyre: Dyre can detect sandbox analysis environments by inspecting the process list and Registry.
Cobalt Strike: The Cobalt Strike loader can use the `MessageBoxA` API to prompt for user interaction as an anti-sandbox measure.
Anchor: Anchor has used NTFS to hide files.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can use spoof arguments in spawned processes that execute beacon commands.

SystemBC: SystemBC has leveraged the Sleep functions before and after commands to ensure execution using the hexadecimal values within commands to include `Sleep(0x2710u)` that waits 10 seconds, and `Sleep(0xEA60u)` for 60 seconds.
Wizard Spider has shut down or uninstalled security applications on victim systems that might prevent ransomware from executing.
Wizard Spider has used Digicert code-signing certificates for some of its malware.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has used the icacls command to modify access control to backup servers, providing them with full control of all the system folders.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCShadow` module can be used to make AD updates by temporarily setting a computer to be a DC.
Wizard Spider has dumped the lsass.exe memory to harvest credentials with the use of open-source tool LaZagne.
TrickBot: TrickBot can obtain passwords stored in files from web browsers such as Chrome, Firefox, Internet Explorer, and Microsoft Edge, sometimes using esentutl.
Wizard Spider has acquired credentials from the SAM/SECURITY registry hives.

TrickBot: TrickBot can obtain passwords stored in files from several applications such as Outlook, Filezilla, OpenSSH, OpenVPN and WinSCP. Additionally, it searches for the ".vnc.lnk" affix to steal VNC credentials.
Wizard Spider has used PowerShell cmdlet `Invoke-WCMDump` to enumerate Windows credentials in the Credential Manager in a compromised network.
Wizard Spider has used Rubeus, MimiKatz Kerberos module, and the Invoke-Kerberoast cmdlet to steal AES hashes.
Wizard Spider has used the Invoke-Inveigh PowerShell cmdlets, likely for name service poisoning.
Rubeus: Rubeus can forge a ticket-granting ticket.
Rubeus: Rubeus can create silver tickets.

Wizard Spider has gained access to credentials via exported copies of the ntds.dit Active Directory database. Wizard Spider has also created a volume shadow copy and used a batch script file to collect NTDS.dit with the use of the Windows utility, ntdsutil.
LaZagne: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from LSA secrets to obtain account and password information.
Emotet: Emotet has been observed to hook network APIs to monitor network traffic.
Empire: Empire includes keylogging capabilities for Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.
TrickBot: TrickBot has the ability to capture RDP credentials by capturing the `CredEnumerateA` API
Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO::Extract` module can extract keys by interacting with Windows cryptographic application programming interface (API) functions.
Wizard Spider has used PowerShell cmdlets `Get-GPPPassword` and `Find-GPOPassword` to find unsecured credentials in a compromised network group policy.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credentials from databases, mail, and WiFi across multiple platforms.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credentials from macOS Keychains.
LaZagne: LaZagne can perform credential dumping from MSCache to obtain account and password information.

Mimikatz: Mimikatz performs credential dumping to obtain account and password information useful in gaining access to additional systems and enterprise network resources. It contains functionality to acquire information about credentials in many ways, including from DCSync/NetSync.

procedures.text: LaZagne: LaZagne can use the `<PID>/maps` and `<PID>/mem` files to identify regex patterns to dump cleartext passwords from the browser's process memory.
LaZagne: LaZagne can obtain credential information from /etc/shadow using the shadow.py module.
Emotet: Emotet has been observed using a hard coded list of passwords to brute force user accounts.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses brute-force attack against RDP with rdpscanDll module.
TrickBot: TrickBot has retrieved PuTTY credentials by querying the `Software\SimonTatham\Putty\Sessions` registry key
TrickBot: TrickBot can steal passwords from the KeePass open source password manager.
Rubeus: Rubeus can reveal the credentials of accounts that have Kerberos pre-authentication disabled through AS-REP roasting.

procedures.text: Mimikatz: Mimikatz's `CRYPTO` module can create and export various types of authentication certificates.

Wizard Spider has used ipconfig to identify the network configuration of a victim machine. Wizard Spider has also used the PowerShell cmdlet `Get-ADComputer` to collect IP address data from Active Directory.

Wizard Spider has used networkdll for network discovery and psfin specifically for financial and point of sale indicators. Wizard Spider has also used AdFind, `nltest/dclist`, and PowerShell script Get-DataInfo.ps1 to enumerate domain computers, including the domain controller.
Wizard Spider has used "whoami" to identify the local user and their privileges.

Wizard Spider has used Systeminfo and similar commands to acquire detailed configuration information of a victim's machine. Wizard Spider has also utilized the PowerShell cmdlet `Get-ADComputer` to collect DNS hostnames, last logon dates, and operating system information from Active Directory.
Wizard Spider has used the “net view” command to locate mapped network shares.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses module networkDll for process list discovery.

TrickBot: TrickBot searches the system for all of the following file extensions:.avi,.mov,.mkv,.mpeg,.mpeg4,.mp4,.mp3,.wav,.ogg,.jpeg,.jpg,.png,.bmp,.gif,.tiff,.ico,.xlsx, and.zip. It can also obtain browsing history, cookies, and plug-in information.

Wizard Spider has identified domain admins through the use of `net group "Domain admins" /DOMAIN`. Wizard Spider has also leveraged the PowerShell cmdlet `Get-ADComputer` to collect account names from Active Directory data.
TrickBot: TrickBot can gather information about domain trusts by utilizing Nltest.
TrickBot: TrickBot collects the users of the system.
TrickBot: TrickBot collects a list of install programs and services on the system’s machine.
Conti: Conti can enumerate routine network connections from a compromised host.
AdFind: AdFind can enumerate domain groups.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has used WMI to identify anti-virus products installed on a victim's machine.
BloodHound: BloodHound can collect information about local groups and members.

SystemBC: SystemBC has leveraged the time of the device to create a text file with a filename that uses the function of `uniqid(time()).‘.txt`, consisting of the 10 character UNIX timestamp and 13 hexadecimal characters.
Bazar: Bazar can query the Registry for installed applications.
Bazar: Bazar can perform a check to ensure that the operating system's keyboard and language settings are not set to Russian.
Bazar: Bazar can query `Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall` for installed applications.
Empire: Empire can perform port scans from an infected host.
TrickBot: TrickBot collects email addresses from Outlook.
Wizard Spider has utilized the PowerShell script `Get-DataInfo.ps1` to collect installed backup software information from a compromised machine.
BloodHound: BloodHound has the ability to collect local admin information via GPO.
Emotet: Emotet can extract names of all locally reachable Wi-Fi networks and then perform a brute-force attack to spread to new networks.
TrickBot: TrickBot can identify the groups the user on a compromised host belongs to.
Net: The `net accounts` and `net accounts /domain` commands with Net can be used to obtain password policy information.
Empire: Empire has the ability to gather browser data such as bookmarks and visited sites.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can identify the country code on a compromised host.
Ryuk: Ryuk has called `GetLogicalDrives` to emumerate all mounted drives, and `GetDriveTypeW` to determine the drive type.
Wizard Spider has used SMB to drop Cobalt Strike Beacon on a domain controller for lateral movement.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has exploited or attempted to exploit Zerologon (CVE-2020-1472) and EternalBlue (MS17-010) vulnerabilities.
Wizard Spider has used the `Invoke-SMBExec` PowerShell cmdlet to execute the pass-the-hash technique and utilized stolen password hashes to move laterally.
Wizard Spider has used stolen credentials to copy tools into the `%TEMP%` directory of domain controllers.
Wizard Spider has used RDP for lateral movement and to deploy ransomware interactively.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has used Window Remote Management to move laterally through a victim network.
Wizard Spider has used the WebDAV protocol to execute Ryuk payloads hosted on network file shares.
Empire: Empire can utilize `Invoke-DCOM` to leverage remote COM execution for lateral movement.
Empire: Empire contains modules for executing commands over SSH as well as in-memory VNC agent injection.
TrickBot: TrickBot has used a VNC module to monitor the victim and collect information to pivot to valuable systems on the network
Conti: Conti can spread itself by infecting other remote machines via network shared drives.
Mimikatz: Mimikatz’s `LSADUMP::DCSync` and `KERBEROS::PTT` modules implement the three steps required to extract the krbtgt account hash and create/use Kerberos tickets.
Wizard Spider has collected data from a compromised host prior to exfiltration.
Wizard Spider has staged ZIP files in local directories such as, `C:\PerfLogs\1\` and `C:\User\1\` prior to exfiltration.
Wizard Spider has collected and staged credentials and network enumeration information, using the networkdll and psfin TrickBot modules.
Empire: Empire is capable of capturing screenshots on Windows and macOS systems.
Emotet: Emotet has been observed leveraging a module that scrapes email data from Outlook.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses web injects and browser redirection to trick the user into providing their login credentials on a fake or modified web page.
BloodHound: BloodHound can compress data collected by its SharpHound ingestor into a ZIP file to be written to disk.
Wizard Spider has archived data into ZIP files on compromised machines.
Emotet: Emotet has been observed leveraging a module that can scrape email addresses from Outlook.
Empire: Empire can harvest clipboard data on both Windows and macOS systems.
Empire: Empire can automatically gather the username, domain name, machine name, and other information from a compromised system.
Empire: Empire can capture webcam data on Windows and macOS systems.
Wizard Spider can transfer malicious payloads such as ransomware to compromised machines.
Wizard Spider has used HTTP for network communications.

TrickBot: TrickBot uses a custom crypter leveraging Microsoft’s CryptoAPI to encrypt C2 traffic.Newer versions of TrickBot have been known to use `bcrypt` to encrypt and digitally sign responses to their C2 server.
TrickBot: TrickBot can Base64-encode C2 commands.
Bazar: Bazar can use TLS in C2 communications.
TrickBot: TrickBot can use secondary C2 servers for communication after establishing connectivity and relaying victim information to primary C2 servers.
SystemBC: SystemBC has used DNS servers to resolve.bit domains to C2 infrastructure.
SystemBC: SystemBC has used raw TCP on non-standard ports, such as 4044, for C2 communications and for HTTP communications, which include downloading binaries.

TrickBot: Some TrickBot samples have used HTTP over ports 447 and 8082 for C2. Newer versions of TrickBot have been known to use a custom communication protocol which sends the data unencrypted over port 443.
SystemBC: SystemBC has encoded with XOR and encrypted with RC4 its beacon.
GrimAgent: GrimAgent can pad C2 messages with random generated values.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can leverage the HTTP protocol for C2 communication, while hiding the actual data in either an HTTP header, URI parameter, the transaction body, or appending it to the URI. Cobalt Strike
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can conduct peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can be configured to have commands relayed over a peer-to-peer network of infected hosts. This can be used to limit the number of egress points, or provide access to a host without direct internet access.
TrickBot: TrickBot has been known to reach a command and control server via one of nine proxy IP addresses.

SystemBC: SystemBC has used multiple proxy layers, such as SOCKS5 and Tor, for C2 communication. SystemBC has also leveraged Tor for encrypting and concealing C2 traffic. The server component of SystemBC has used SOCKS5 for C2 communication.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike has the ability to accept a value for HTTP Host Header to enable domain fronting.
Bazar: Bazar downloads have been hosted on Google Docs.
Empire: Empire can use Dropbox and GitHub for C2.
Bazar: The Bazar loader is used to download and execute the Bazar backdoor.
TrickBot: TrickBot uses vncDll module to remote control the victim machine.
Bazar: Bazar can implement DGA using the current date as a seed variable.

Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike uses a custom command and control protocol that is encapsulated in HTTP, HTTPS, or DNS. In addition, it conducts peer-to-peer communication over Windows named pipes encapsulated in the SMB protocol. All protocols use their standard assigned ports.
Emotet: Emotet has encrypted data before sending to the C2 server.
Wizard Spider has exfiltrated domain credentials and network enumeration information over command and control (C2) channels.
Wizard Spider has exfiltrated victim information using FTP.

procedures.text: Wizard Spider has exfiltrated stolen victim data to various cloud storage providers.
Empire: Empire has the ability to automatically send collected data back to the threat actors' C2.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike can set its Beacon payload to reach out to the C2 server on an arbitrary and random interval.
Cobalt Strike: Cobalt Strike will break large data sets into smaller chunks for exfiltration.
Empire: Empire can use GitHub for data exfiltration.
Wizard Spider has used taskkill.exe and net.exe to stop backup, catalog, cloud, and other services prior to network encryption.
Wizard Spider has used WMIC and vssadmin to manually delete volume shadow copies. Wizard Spider has also used Conti ransomware to delete volume shadow copies automatically with the use of vssadmin.

Ryuk: Ryuk has used a combination of symmetric (AES) and asymmetric (RSA) encryption to encrypt files. Files have been encrypted with their own AES key and given a file extension of.RYK. Encrypted directories have had a ransom note of RyukReadMe.txt written to the directory.
Ryuk: An enterprise resource planning (ERP) manufacturing server was lost to the Ryuk attack. The manufacturing process had to rely on paper and existing orders to keep the shop floor open.
Diavol: Diavol can delete specified files from a targeted system.

Diavol: After encryption, Diavol will capture the desktop background window, set the background color to black, and change the desktop wallpaper to a newly created bitmap image with the text “All your files are encrypted! For more information see “README-FOR-DECRYPT.txt".
TrickBot: TrickBot module "Trickboot" can write or erase the UEFI/BIOS firmware of a compromised device.
